about: Lane KAUDIT coverage table (2026-10-25): how far the public knowledge bundle covers the wet lab (chemistry, biology, materials/batteries). One cell per row of the brief's table; each cell has 3-5 questions a researcher would ask during a run (mostly Korean, some English, some without a question mark), written before the bundle was searched, and the bundle pieces that answer each one, read and checked, or why none does. Measured by scripts/public_knowledge_audit.py map.

fields.areas: the brief's areas, in its order
fields.cells[].importance: safety: how much harm a wrong or missing answer can do (3 high); use: how often a wet lab meets it (3 every week). Lane KAUDIT's estimate, used only to order the gaps; a person may change it
fields.cells[].terms: words that mark a piece as about the cell, for counting related pieces (Latin-letter terms match whole words, case ignored; Hangul terms as substrings)
fields.cells[].coverage_note: what the bundle holds and lacks for the cell, in one line (written while finding the gold pieces)
fields.questions[].gold: pieces that answer the question: source_id ('*' for any) and title_contains / locator_contains / text_contains substrings (whitespace collapsed, case ignored); found when any matching piece is in the top five
fields.questions[].no_answer: why no piece answers (when gold is empty): the bundle was searched with several words and the search
fields.questions[].in_pubchem_list: reagent cells only: whether the reagent asked about is in data/public_knowledge/pubchem_compounds.txt

verdict_rule: ✓ when at least two thirds of a cell's questions find a gold piece in the server-style top five; ✗ when no question has any gold piece in the bundle; △ otherwise (some found, or material there but not found)
